name: Chi Protocol

Attacker flash-loaned 5 WETH from Balancer, bought depegged USC cheaply from thin Uniswap V2 pool, burned it 1:1 at par against ReserveHolder to redeem full-value weETH/stETH/WETH collateral, netting ~4.66 WETH. descriptions.text: ArbitrageV5.burn() redeems reserve collateral valuing USC at hardcoded $1 with no peg check (unlike mint which enforces peg). Attacker flash-loaned 5 WETH from Balancer, bought depegged USC cheaply from thin Uniswap V2 pool, burned it 1:1 at par against ReserveHolder to redeem full-value weETH/stETH/WETH collateral, netting ~4.66 WETH. Attack Tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0x4a665f8eeada74552bd2dc466e5549731951f2f6180bbe865fa1d7b4be8ae96f Source: https://twitter.com/DefimonAlerts/status/2076887008773829119

Chi Protocol (a DeFi stablecoin protocol issuing $USC backed by LSTs/LRTs on Ethereum) was exploited due to a logic error in the ArbitrageV5 contract’s burn() function. The attacker used a flash loan to buy heavily depegged $USC cheaply on a thin Uniswap V2 pool and burned it to redeem full-value collateral (weETH/stETH/WETH) at the hardcoded $1 peg, without the burn function checking the actual peg (unlike the mint function). This resulted in approximately $8,500 loss, nearly draining the protocol’s reserves.

On July 13, 2026, Chi Protocol on Ethereum Mainnet lost approximately $8,500 due to a logic flaw in its redemption mechanism. The attacker bought depegged USC tokens cheaply, then redeemed them for full-value collateral using a burn() logic error. The ArbitrageV5 contract's burn() function allowed users to redeem USC stablecoins for collateral at a fixed $1 rate without checking if the token was still pegged at $1, letting an attacker profit by redeeming depegged tokens for more collateral than they were worth.
